title: Introduce RAG Testbench and Tool-Fabric Quickstart for local harnessing
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new local quickstart: a lightweight RAG testbench and pluggable tool-fabric for iterative dev and telemetry-driven validation.
description:
Summary: Introduces an opinionated local quickstart (examples/rag-testbench) that combines a RAG harness, an extensible 'tool-fabric' for binding tools at runtime, and a small validation suite to exercise retrieval/answering workflows. This is targeted at developer onboarding and reproducible QA for RAG integrations.

Motivation: Teams repeatedly rebuild similar scaffolding to test retrieval prompts, tool-calling flows, and model/embedding variants. This quickstart provides a batteries-included sandbox (Docker + node/python adapters) so engineers can iterate on prompts, swap retrieval backends, and run small regression checks with telemetry. It is intentionally minimal compared to production infra and focuses on fast feedback loops and telemetry-friendly artifacts.

What changed:
- New example: examples/rag-testbench/ - README, Docker compose, node and python adapters for the tool-fabric, a small in-memory vector store shim, and a tiny web REPL for interactive sessions.
- docs/quickstarts/rag-testbench.md - step-by-step guide and patterns for migrating from the sandbox to more robust deployments.
- scripts/validate-rag.sh - lightweight validation runner for CI or local use; executes a curated set of prompts against a pinned model and reports precision/recall-ish metrics and latency distributions.
- ci/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml - adds a non-blocking smoke job to verify the example boots and the validation runner completes.
- minor edits to examples/README_INDEX.md to register the new quickstart.

Usage (local quickstart):
1) git checkout feature/rag-testbench-tool-fabric-quickstart
2) cd examples/rag-testbench && docker-compose up --build
3) open http://localhost:8080 to launch the REPL; use /tools to bind tool implementations from tool-fabric/adapters/*
4) Run the validation runner: ./scripts/validate-rag.sh --model local-redwood:serve --prompts test/prompts.yaml

Tool-Fabric design notes:
- Tool descriptors are plain JSON files in examples/rag-testbench/tool-fabric/descriptors/; adapters implement an adapter interface (lightweight) and register via a manifest. The fabric supports hot-reload for rapid iteration.
- Adapters included: http_call_adapter (Node), sql_stub_adapter (Python), file_lookup_adapter (Node). These are intentionally simplistic but illustrate how tool results are normalized for the aggregator.

Tests and CI: The smoke workflow spins up the Docker stack, runs the validation runner against a pinned local model image (mock/stubbed in CI) and reports pass/fail. The first CI run failed due to a timing race in the REPL bootstrap; I added a retry/backoff to the healthcheck and reran — subsequent runs passed. The ci_status is recorded above.

Review notes (conversation highlights):
- Diego Ruiz: "Can the test runner output structured telemetry (JSON) to be consumed by the Optimize team?"
  - Author: "Added --output-json flag to scripts/validate-rag.sh; writes metrics/trace to artifacts/validation.json. Marked in docs.
- Sofia Patel: "Can we make adapters smaller and importable as packages for reuse?"
  - Author: "Adapters are structured to be lightweight and easily extracted; added a README on packaging adapters and examples of API surface.
- Liam O'Connor: "CI smoke job should be non-blocking on main — we don't want example flakiness to block merges."
  - Author: "Marked ci/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml as optional and non-blocking. Also reduced resource footprint.

Backward compatibility and risk: No API changes to core Redwood libraries. This is purely example and docs, low risk. The quickstart intentionally uses minimal pinned versions and a stubbed vector store so it won't interfere with infra.
